_README: The ISL pin this repo's PLoT -> ISL request drift pairing is derived against.
Contract step-2 slice 2. Hand-edited ONLY when deliberately re-pinning ISL.
RE-PINNING PROCEDURE (all four steps, in order — the standing test fails if
any is skipped, which is the point):
1. Fresh blobless clone of the ISL repo at the new sha, OUTSIDE this repo.
asserts that the committed replay transcript was generated against exactly
this pin (transcript.pin_digest == sha256 of the canonical form of this file).
Bumping the pin without re-running the driver therefore turns the suite RED
instead of leaving a pairing silently derived against stale bytes.

isl.pinned_by: ROADMAP 2.749 deliberate re-pin, 2026-08-06 (11 commits: ISL #118-#126 + 2.720 + 2.704). The previous pin (35149dd1, 1 Aug) PREDATED goal_threshold_frame, which PLoT ALREADY SENDS (translator-v3.ts:767, ROADMAP 2.258) — so the pairing was derived against bytes in which a field PLoT emits was UNDECLARED and would have been silently dropped by extra='ignore'. The gate never went RED on it only because no egress producer builds a goal-stamped body; that coverage gap is the finding, not the pin. Also adopted here: user_stated_ranges (2.720, ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-07 — this note said 'PLoT does not send it' and that is NO LONGER TRUE: PLoT now sends it from /v2/run via the request-gated branch in toISLRobustnessRequest, and the `v2-run-user-stated-ranges` producer walks ISL's whole UserStatedRange class against this pin. The SHA is unchanged — only the sentence was stale, which is trap 14 exactly: a note that was accurate when written and became the most convincing wrong thing in the file), and on the response side OutcomeDistributionV2.mean/std required -> optional (ISL #125 / 2.477(a)) which PLoT's consumers and types already handle. Re-pinned alone, no behaviour change: ROADMAP 2.744's lane deliberately did NOT bump so its defect fix would not smuggle an unrelated contract change.

runtime.why_these: src/config/__init__.py imports pydantic_settings as a package-init side effect, and src/utils/correlation.py imports numpy at module scope. Both are hard requirements of merely IMPORTING RobustnessRequestV2 — neither is obvious from the model file.

isl_openapi_json.what_it_is: ISL's committed, MACHINE-GENERATED OpenAPI document (scripts/generate_openapi.py -> FastAPI app.openapi()). It is Pydantic's own description of the mounted request models, not a hand-written copy — which is why the pairing may consume it hermetically. ISL CI (.github/workflows/openapi-validation.yml) runs `generate_openapi.py --check` on every PR touching src/api, src/models, pyproject or the spec, so it cannot drift from the models without ISL going red.
isl_openapi_json.what_it_is_NOT: It is not evidence about DEPLOYED ISL. It describes the app as built at this sha.

source_sha256._note: The model + router files every claim in the pairing is derived from. The Python replay driver verifies each of these against the clone it is pointed at and REFUSES to run on a mismatch, so a transcript can never be produced from bytes other than these. Review S4: src/api/robustness.py is pinned too — the mounted_request_models handler cite names a LINE in it, and a hand-maintained line number in another repo drifts silently. It drifted again at this re-pin (2.749): analyze_robustness_v2 578 -> 579 -> 582, analyze_counterfactual 255 -> 263. RE-DERIVE every line cite in this file at each re-pin; never carry one forward. src/models/range_fit.py was ADDED to this list at the 2.749 re-pin: robustness_v2.py and response_v2.py now import UserStatedRange / RangeFitDisclosure from it (ROADMAP 2.720), so it is load-bearing for BOTH the request and the response closure — without an entry here it could change without the pin noticing, which is the exact hole this list exists to close.

mounted_request_models._note: Route -> request model, for the paths PLoT sends to. Derived from src/api/main.py include_router() calls + the router-level path decorators, and corroborated independently by the vendored openapi.json path list.

/api/v1/robustness/analyze/v2.extra_policy: ignore (explicit on all 11 classes in the tree)

/api/v1/causal/counterfactual.extra_policy: pydantic default (unset) — same runtime behaviour as ignore, but NOT a declared contract
